topicData.topic: Can an enterprise outsource its AI transformation without outsourcing its future capability?
topicData.angle: Write from the specific details and your honest reaction to this topic.

postText:
Outsourcing your AI transformation is fine. Outsourcing your ability to understand what's happening to your own business is a different thing entirely.

A major AI partnership was announced this week. Big names. Big ambitions. It raised a question for me: who inside the organisation is actually building capability through it?

The vendor will build the models, run the pilots, ship the dashboards. Eighteen months later when the contract ends or the strategy shifts, what capability actually stayed behind? What does the internal team now know that they didn't before?

This is the thing nobody says out loud when the contract gets signed.

Outsourcing payroll doesn't change how your organisation thinks. AI transformation, done entirely by an external team, might. Because the understanding of why a model behaves the way it does, what data it's actually surfacing, where it's failing quietly — that understanding has to live somewhere internal or it doesn't live at all.

I've watched this play out differently depending on the sector. In a telecoms operator, the risk sits in network operations. The vendor delivers the tool. The engineers who run the network don't fully understand it anymore. That's a capability gap with real consequences. In a facilities management firm the same dynamic shows up in contract performance, in the data that feeds client SLAs, in decisions that get made by people who no longer fully own the logic behind them.

Different industries. Same structural problem.

And I genuinely don't have a clean answer here. Maybe hybrid delivery models work. Maybe embedding the right people deeply enough into the vendor team is sufficient. Maybe the question of what stays behind needs to be in the contract, not the retrospective.

But if that question isn't being asked loudly before the ink dries, someone should be asking it.

If you've been in the room when one of these deals got signed, what did you see happen to internal capability twelve months later?

#AILeadership #EnterpriseStrategy #TechLeadership
